name: Basil
summary: The summer herb for pesto, tomatoes and salads. Loves heat, hates cold.
problems: Turns black after nights below about 10 °C (50 °F). Downy mildew causes yellowing with gray fuzz under leaves; resistant varieties help.
greenhouse_notes: Grows year round in a warm greenhouse or a sunny window.
notes: Pinch off flower buds and the tips of stems to keep plants bushy and leafy. Freeze pesto in ice cube trays for winter.

name: Cilantro
summary: Fresh leaves for salsa and tacos, and coriander seed once it flowers. A cool-weather herb.
problems: Bolts quickly in heat and long days. Sow a little every two to three weeks in cool weather.
notes: Let some plants flower: the seeds are coriander, and the flowers feed helpful insects. Fallen seed often comes up on its own in fall.

name: Dill
summary: Feathery leaves and seed heads for pickles. Feeds swallowtail caterpillars and helpful insects.
problems: Doesn't transplant well; sow it where it will grow. Bolts in heat.
notes: Time a sowing to flower when your cucumbers are ready, so seed heads are fresh for pickling.

name: Parsley
summary: Flat-leaf or curly, it keeps going for months and through light frosts.
problems: Seeds are very slow to sprout; soak them overnight first. Swallowtail caterpillars may share it with you.
notes: A biennial: it leafs up the first year and flowers the second. Cut outer stems at the base and leave the center growing.

name: Oregano
summary: A tough perennial for sauces and drying. Comes back every year with little care.
problems: Rots in wet, heavy soil; it likes it lean and well drained. Flavor fades if it's overwatered or fed too much.
notes: Buying a small plant or a division from a friend is faster than seed. Cut stems just before flowering for the strongest flavor, and dry them in bundles.
